text:
Casey Cizikas has played 999 NHL games, every one of them for the Islanders, a fourth-round pick in 2009 who never wore another jersey. The milestone headlines have been about the journey, with Yahoo Sports quoting him that it "hasn't been easy." At 35, he remains what he has been for a decade: a fourth-line center whose job is to keep the puck away from his net.

The scoring has thinned, with 4 points in 21 games at about 12 minutes a night and one goal, below the 10 he scored last season. His shooting is at 7%, well under league average, so a couple more goals would be normal. But nobody keeps Cizikas around for offense.

The defense still holds up. The Islanders win a slight edge in expected goals at five on five with him on, better than their rate without him. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer expected chances with him out there last season, in the 96th percentile of forwards. His next game will be his 1,000th, a rare number for a career built in one city on the bottom line.
headline: Cizikas, one game short of 1,000
